CreateDeploymentStacksWhatIfResult builds a default stack resource ID using azureContext.Subscription.Id when StackResourceId is not provided. But azureContext is only set when DeploymentStacksWhatIfSdkClient is created with the IAzureContext constructor. If the client is created with the IDeploymentStacksClient constructor, azureContext can be null, which could cause a NullReferenceException.
This preserves both constructor paths and keeps the IDeploymentStacksClient constructor usable for tests or injected clients. It only requires IAzureContext when the code actually needs to infer a subscription-scoped stack resource ID. If the caller provides StackResourceId, or if the scope is management group, no subscription context is needed. This avoids a confusing NullReferenceException and gives an actionable error message.
